monster_dango_bit_idle.png.prompt:
The attached reference image is the PARENT monster: a pale pink dango-slime made of soft round rice-dumpling lumps stuck together, with a bamboo skewer through it.

This picture must show ONE SMALL PIECE that broke off that parent, so a player must instantly recognise it as a chunk of the same creature. Copy from the reference exactly:
- the SAME pale, milky, desaturated pink (NOT a saturated hot pink)
- the SAME soft MATTE finish with gentle rounded shading (NOT a glossy shiny ball, no big white highlight)
- the SAME thick black outline weight and the same flat-colour cartoon style
- the SAME face language: simple thin curved closed eyes, tiny mouth, small soft pink blush ovals
- the SAME squishy dough silhouette with little soft lumps and a slightly melting bottom edge

What is different: it is ONE single dumpling lump instead of a cluster, about a third of the parent's size, and a SHORT BROKEN STUB of the bamboo skewer is still stuck in its top - that snapped stub is the clue that it came off the big one.

Pose: sitting still and slightly squashed, content, thin curved closed eyes, tiny closed smile, wobbling gently in place

Full body, standing on the very bottom edge of the picture. Nothing else in the picture: no ground line, no shadow, no scenery, no text, no letters, no watermark.
Draw everything SOLID and OPAQUE - flat filled colour with soft shading. Nothing transparent.
Background must be a solid pure green (#00FF00), completely flat, for chroma keying. Nothing green on the creature.
Output 1024x1024 PNG. Save the image as monster_dango_bit_idle.png in the current directory and report the path.
